paper_metadata.title: Quantum Algorithm for Local-Volatility Option Pricing via the Kolmogorov Equation

summary: The paper proposes a gate-based quantum algorithm that solves the Kolmogorov forward PDE for option pricing via Schrödingerisation and Hamiltonian simulation. Theoretical analysis claims quantum gate complexity O(N^2 polylog N) compared to classical O(N^3) finite-difference or exponential-integration methods for N=2^n grid points, with multidimensional scaling O(d^5). No hardware or simulator experiments are performed.

experiments.description: Gate-based quantum algorithm for pricing European vanilla options under a local-volatility model by solving the Kolmogorov forward PDE via Schrödingerisation, time-dependent Hamiltonian simulation, and swap-test-based payoff recovery; includes single-asset and multi-asset scaling analysis.

algorithm.variant: Schrödingerisation-based Hamiltonian simulation for the Kolmogorov forward equation with clock-dimension embedding

hyperparameters.volatility_parameterization: polynomial in space and time, sigma(s,t)=sum_{k=0..D_s} sum_{q=0..D_t} C_kq s^k t^q

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Price distribution p(s,t) encoded into amplitudes of an n-qubit register; initial condition approximated by computational basis state |S0> or sharply peaked Gaussian; auxiliary Schrödingerisation and clock registers discretize additional qumodes
problem_formulation.objective_function: Compute option price V(0)=e^{-rT} E[C0(S_T)] by evolving the forward Kolmogorov PDE and recovering the expected payoff via overlap estimation
problem_formulation.constraints_handling: Post-selection on positive momentum eigenvectors; swap test for overlap estimation
problem_formulation.problem_hamiltonian: Time-dependent pseudo-Hamiltonian H_LV embedded into time-independent H = I⊗I_w⊗p_y + H_LVS(t=x_y)

problem_instance.description: European vanilla call/put option pricing under a local-volatility model; includes single-asset pricing and a d-asset extension for basket-style scaling analysis

dataset_specification.description: Model-based local-volatility surface; no market dataset specified

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: No empirical dataset preprocessing; volatility surface assumed polynomially approximable and discretized on a uniform grid
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Theoretical complexity analysis; illustrative Black-Scholes overlap plots; no numerical benchmark protocol or repeated-run statistics reported

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Classical discretization of the PDE on a uniform grid; polynomial approximation of volatility; construction of payoff state and normalization factors
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Swap-test estimation of overlaps to recover option price; post-selection on positive momentum; normalization via a second swap test with |+>^n
classical_baselines: Classical finite-difference time stepping with O(s T N^3) complexity
Classical exponential-integration / matrix-exponential action with O(s T N^3) complexity

results.value: O((s||H||_max T + log(1/eps_evol)/log(e + log(1/eps_evol)/(s||H||_max T))) * [D_s n log n + s n + n_w log n_w + D_t n_y log n_y])
O((gamma + log(gamma/eps_evol)/log log(gamma/eps_evol)) * (n + n_w + n_y + m polylog(m)))

speedup_claims.factor: polynomial speedup in grid size; summarized as O(N^2 polylog N) vs O(N^3)
speedup_claims.baseline_method: classical finite-difference time stepping and exponential-integration methods
speedup_claims.conditions: single-asset discretization; gate-based Hamiltonian simulation with block-encoding and Schrödingerisation; asymptotic scaling
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper states the speedup is polynomial, not exponential, for a single asset; the dominant restriction is the discretized momentum operator norm scaling as 2^(2n).

speedup_claims.factor: exponential speedup in dimension / mitigation of curse of dimensionality
speedup_claims.caveats: The paper presents scaling analysis rather than a numerical benchmark; the claimed advantage is in dimension d, with evolution cost O(d^5) and initial-state preparation O(dn).

speedup_claims.factor: quadratic improvement in retrieval via forward formulation versus backward amplitude-encoding retrieval
speedup_claims.conditions: when recovering option price from expected value using swap test
speedup_claims.caveats: This is a qualitative advantage of the forward formulation; no direct benchmark numbers are reported.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: Hamiltonian simulation gate complexity O((s||H||_max T + log(1/eps_evol)/log(e + log(1/eps_evol)/(s||H||_max T))) * [D_s n log n + s n + n_w log n_w + D_t n_y log n_y]); overall option-pricing scaling summarized as O(N^2 polylog N) for N=2^n grid points; multi-asset evolution cost O(d^5) in dimension d
complexity_analysis.classical_complexity: O(s T N^3) for both finite-difference time stepping and exponential-integration methods

advantage_assessment.crossover_size: Not reported; asymptotic comparison only (O(N^2 polylog N) vs O(N^3))
advantage_assessment.resources_for_advantage: Requires large logical registers (n + n_w + n_y qubits), block-encoded Hamiltonian simulation, and accurate swap-test overlap estimation; no concrete qubit counts or fault-tolerant resource estimates provided.
limiting_factors: Hamiltonian norm dominated by discretized momentum operator scaling as 2^(2n)
Requires fault-tolerant Hamiltonian simulation and block encoding
Amplitude encoding and state preparation overhead
No hardware demonstration or realistic resource estimates
Speedup is only polynomial in grid size for single-asset problems

notes: No specific hardware platform or simulator is named; the paper is a theoretical gate-based algorithm paper.
The paper reports gate-complexity expressions and CNOT counts for subroutines, but not a single end-to-end transpiled depth or execution on hardware.
The paper explicitly states a polynomial advantage in grid size (O(N^2 polylog N) vs classical O(N^3)) and potential exponential improvement with dimension for basket options.
However, no numerical experiments, hardware runs, or crossover estimates are provided.
